newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU may close grain tax window for Thursday tender.
newsitem.headline: EU may close grain tax window for Thursday tender.

text.p: A European Union rule scrapping taxes at weekly grain export tenders may be published on Wednesday, in time for Thursday's auction, but any delay would push the policy change back to next week, EU sources said.

The timing of the announcement, formalising a decision last week to stop accepting tax offers at the tenders held each Thursday, is crucial to traders because even publication on Thursday morning would be too late for that day's tender.

Even though exporters have still been able to bid for subsidies while the EU was encouraging taxes, traders say the tax window's continued existence despite a plunge in world prices has made it harder for subsidy bids to succeed.
"The regulation will be published tomorrow (Wednesday) or the day after tomorrow," an EU source told Reuters.
"If it is published tomorrow, everyone takes part in a tender for subsidies. If it's Thursday, then the tender is open for both taxes and restitutions," the source said.

The EU took the rare decision to charge taxes for its wheat and barley exports last December after world grain markets soared above the price paid to Europe's protected farmers for the first time in 20 years.
But after hiting all-time highs in April, grain markets have dropped sharply, due mainly to a rebound in production.

Traders have been campaigning for the rules to be clarified so that they can bid for the traditional subsidies without seeing their competitors offering up high taxes and preventing the European Commission from accepting their own bids.
The Commission traditionally attempts to limit the spread between the highest and lowest bids accepted, so that a tax offer by one trader makes another's subsidy bid likely to fail.
A separate regulation scrapping the standing wheat export tax of 10 Ecus per tonne payable through an alternative daily channel will be published on Friday or Monday, EU sources said.
